spans.s: सगण [sagaṇa], a. Attended by troops or flocks. -णः An epithet of Śiva.
सगतिक [sagatika], a. Connected with a preposition &c.
Proud, arrogant. -न्धः A kinsman, relation, kindred; सर्वः सगन्धेषु विश्वसिति Ś.5;

सगर [sagara], a. [गरेण विषेण सहितः] Poisonous, having poison, -रः N. of a king of the Solar race. [He was a son of Bāhu and was called Sagara because he was born together with gara or poison given to his mother by the other wife of his father. By his wife Sumati he had 6 sons. He successfully performed 99 sacrifices but when he commenced the hundredth, his sacrificial horse was stolen by Indra and carried down to the Pātāla. Sagara thereupon commanded his 6 sons to search it out. Finding no trace of the animal on earth they began to dig down towards the Pātāla, and in doing this they naturally increased the boundaries of the ocean which was therefore called Sāgara; cf.

. Meeting with the sage Kapila they rashly accused him of having stolen their horse, as a punishment for which they were instantly reduced to ashes by that sage. It whas after several thousands of years that Bhagīratha (q. v.) succeeded in bringing down to the Pātāla the celestial river Ganges to water and purify their ashes and thus to convey their souls to heaven.]
सगर्भः [sagarbhḥ] र्भ्यः [rbhyḥ], र्भ्यः 1 A brother of whole blood; सह तनुज- सगर्भप्रेष्यरक्षःसहस्रैः
Similar to; रत्नावली- श्चौषधिभिः सगर्भाः Bu.
Furnished with a string (as a bow).
Possessed of the qualities in rhetoric.
सगोत्र [sagōtra], a. Being of the same family or kin, related.
त्रः A kinsman sprung from a common ancestor; तत्रभवतो युष्मत्सगोत्रस्य कण्वस्यापराद्धो$स्मि Ś.7.
A kinsman of the same family, one connected by funeral oblations of food and water.
A distant kinsman. -तम् Family, race, lineage.
The ocean, sea; सागरः सागरोपमः; (fig. also); दयासागर, विद्यासागर &c.; cf. सगर.
N. of Bhagīratha; शंकरस्य जटाजूटाद् भ्रष्टां सागरतेजसा
